question: 두 고전적 relative primary 축약 뒤, 허용 경계상태에서 규제 잔여항과 관측가능량·내적·CPT 접합을 함께 판정하려면 어떤 양자 경계 객체와 검사가 먼저 필요한가?

objects.label: 두 고전적 relative primary 축약
objects.summary: M: Pi=bar c=0 및 P(N0): N=N0, rho=0는 선언한 고전적 chart에서 Q, alpha, Omega와 두 relative endpoint 항을 같은 minimal/matter quotient로 내린다.

objects.label: bulk 축약 후 남는 두 endpoint 자료
objects.summary: Local CMW primary split 뒤 action의 -[sigma-plus rho]와 BV-cotangent의 [sigma-plus delta N]은 함께 남으며, bulk doublet 소거만으로 state-space equivalence가 되지 않는다.

objects.label: source-compatible quantum boundary tuple
objects.summary: For each X=M,P, declare graded carrier and invariant domain, polarization, measure/half-density, ghost/Berezin orientation, residual and gauge-fixing data, and quantum BFV differential. This is the first object that lets the established classical quotient maps r_M,r_P become a question about quantum states.

objects.label: actual quantum comparison maps U_M and U_P
objects.summary: A degree-zero comparison must have a declared source and target domain and satisfy U_X D_X subset D_red and Omega_hat_red U_X=U_X Omega_hat_X there. Classical r_M,r_P are not these maps.

objects.label: support와 dualization이 바꾸는 cohomology
objects.summary: The declared compact-N primary complex has H0=H1=0 and infinite-dimensional H2, while a specified same-degree continuous coefficient dual has zero top cohomology; degree-reversed graded-dual detectors are a third object. A carrier name alone does not identify a physical state space.

objects.label: allowed boundary-state pair and limiting topology
objects.summary: Name the left/right test or dual state spaces, their boundary traces, bosonic/Berezin pairing, and the weak or stronger topology before reading a regulated Ward functional as zero, nonzero distribution, or nonconvergence.

objects.label: fixed-box a=2 Green face flux
objects.summary: For the declared real compact test pairing reaching only a=2, the Gaussian Ward limit is a boundary Green form. It may vanish under declared common Dirichlet/real Robin jets or be nonzero on another allowed pair; this does not settle other faces or a physical state family.

objects.label: residual-after-action decision record
objects.summary: For one declared test pair and removal order, record whether the paired residual tends to zero, a nonzero boundary distribution, or fails to converge. Finite positive regulator width is not itself the decision.

objects.label: positive physical product with observable common domain
objects.summary: A physical product requires a chosen constrained or rigged state carrier, positivity/completion, and observables plus adjoints preserving a common domain. Dual evaluation or a complex-bilinear Green form does not provide it.

objects.label: CPT-compatible identity-cylinder datum
objects.summary: A left/right polarization pairing, half-density and ordered ghost Fourier kernel, interval kernel and anti-linear convention must satisfy the distributional BFV intertwining and gluing normalization on the same domains.

objects.label: positive CPT-like label weight의 비선택성
objects.summary: Declared Cauchy-label exchange, positivity and W covariance admit arbitrary smooth positive weights in their stated scope. Symmetry covariance alone therefore does not select a physical product or vacuum.

objects.label: first bounded falsifiable domain audit
objects.summary: Fix one candidate quantum boundary tuple and one X in {M,P}; either exhibit an allowed vector for which U_X leaves the target domain or its BFV chain defect has nonzero pairing, or report that the tuple needed to state the test is absent.

links.label: classical quotient maps become quantum questions only with analytic data
links.explanation: The common classical quotient fixes neither carrier nor measure, so it cannot itself act on a quantum boundary state.
links.falsifier: A source-compatible quantization theorem that supplies all tuple roles directly from the stated classical data would make this missing-object diagnosis too strong.

links.label: declared carriers expose the actual comparison obligation
links.explanation: Only after source and target domains are declared can one ask whether the reduction is a BFV chain map or preserves cohomology.
links.falsifier: An explicit source-to-target quantum construction with a proven intertwining identity and no extra analytic choices would supersede this route.

links.label: cohomology depends on the carrier, support and dual convention
links.explanation: A map cannot be called an equivalence until its support, topology, ghost degree and induced cohomology map are tested on named spaces.
links.falsifier: A named map with a proof of quasi-isomorphism on the declared carriers removes this obstruction for that datum.

links.label: a finite-width residual becomes a decision only after pairing
links.explanation: The same local face flux has declared zero and nonzero instances; the regulator conclusion therefore belongs to a state pair, topology and removal order.
links.falsifier: A uniform operator or distributional convergence theorem over the proposed state family would make individual-pair testing unnecessary in that family.

links.label: CPT sewing is a compatibility test of product, domains and kernel
links.explanation: An anti-linear sign table or formal endpoint delta does not establish the identity-cylinder intertwining or gluing normalization.
links.falsifier: A fully specified kernel with a proven BFV intertwining and normalized gluing on the stated physical product discharges this relation for that construction.

links.label: CPT-like covariance does not choose a weight
links.explanation: A CPT-compatible product still needs an additional source, observable, or selection principle; covariance alone leaves a weight family.
links.falsifier: A derivation from the declared source that fixes one weight while preserving the stated covariance would remove this particular nonselection.
